text: Dr Syed Harun asked about systems integration plans to support Healthier SG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To facilitate holistic, integrated and coordinated care provided by multiple healthcare providers across hospital-based and community care settings, we need to simplify how our healthcare providers access and share data.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The importance of a well-integrated and reliable IT system to connect healthcare providers has been highlighted by many GPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It serves as a centralised repository of key health information that healthcare professionals can access and can contribute to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Its capabilities will be enhanced to cater to a wider spectrum of care providers in a safe and secure manner, enabling healthcare providers in different care settings to make better decisions when caring for their patients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Specific to primary care, we have supported GP clinics and their IT vendors to upgrade their IT systems, to simplify administrative processes and to improve data flows, while ensuring data sharing is secure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, under Healthier SG, we have rolled out the Clinic Management System Tiering Framework for Primary Care to ensure that IT systems used by private GP clinics are integrated with national programmes, for a more seamless delivery of care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also enhanced our national digital health app, HealthHub, to empower residents to manage their own health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through HealthHub, residents can enrol for Healthier SG, view their personalised health plans, manage medical appointments and view their health screening results and vaccination records.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We plan to expand the type of health records available through HealthHub in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Ms Mariam Jaafar suggested making use of technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to optimise healthcare delivery for cost effectiveness and improved patient outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our healthcare institutions use proven, cost-effective technology extensively to automate manual tasks and augment clinical decision-making.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, the Outpatient Pharmacy Automation System helps to automate packing and dispensing of pharmacy medication.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Patients can also utilise HealthHub to arrange for medicine refills and manage their medical appointments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This all helps to reduce waiting times and enhance the patient experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH is also exploring the use of AI-assisted radiology diagnosis systems for pathology detection, to automate the analysis of medical images, support clinicians to identify patients with urgent care needs and help radiologists to generate radiology reports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Wan Rizal suggested utilising AI to improve the accessibility of mental health care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Currently, Mindline employs an AI-enabled chatbot that allows people to share their emotional struggles anonymously and guides them to self-help resources such as psychotherapy exercises and counselling services where needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: While we embrace innovation and leverage technology, patient safety remains of paramount importance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH will continue to evaluate these new technologies for clinical and cost effectiveness and assess their safety and suitability for various uses in our healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked for an update on value-based care initiatives that have been piloted and whether these initiatives have been scaled up across the healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH has been placing increasing emphasis on value-based care efforts since 2015.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These efforts aim to improve health outcomes while simultaneously managing the attendant cost increases in a sustainable way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These initiatives range from national system initiatives to programmes that target individual doctors and specific procedures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government and healthcare providers will provide quality healthcare to residents, but individual responsibility is crucial.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Each of us must take charge of their own health, adopt healthier behaviours, build relationships with our family doctors and proactively manage any chronic diseases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Concurrently, healthcare providers will re-orientate towards preventive care, while the Government sets up systems, programmes and incentives to support healthcare providers in delivering care to residents in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the future, through the Government's efforts in strengthening preventive care and a shift in residents' health-seeking behaviour, the aim is for all of us to visit a regular family doctor as a first point-of-contact and for ongoing support to holistically manage our own health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Together, all of us, everyone, can play a part in improving our health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, let me begin with healthcare manpower.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Dr Syed Harun has rightly pointed out that healthcare manpower needs to keep pace with the growing demand for healthcare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We factor in population needs into the planning of our healthcare manpower.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to grow our healthcare workforce sustainably, while moderating demand through innovative ways of delivering care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To this end, we will continue to work with public healthcare institutions (PHIs) and the community care sector to attract and retain manpower across the board.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This would allow us to improve the attractiveness of the profession and retain the nurses we have.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are engaging Allied Health Professionals to better understand their needs and to co-create the vision for their professions, with a view to come up with a National Allied Health Strategy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are working on the PharmForce initiative to look into manpower development, shaping pharmacy practice to meet population needs, promoting wellness and building resilience of our pharmacy workforce and increasing visibility and recognition for the profession.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Operations and support staff play important roles in our public healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our healthcare clusters have embarked on job redesign initiatives to enhance the career value proposition and better attract and retain them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Across the board, PHIs will continue to keep salaries competitive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have done the same for the community care sector with the recent salary guidelines to keep salaries competitive and provide greater transparency to jobseekers and workers in the sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These guidelines will be reviewed regularly to ensure that they are up-to-date.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We hope that the guidelines will help attract and retain workers across all job groups, including support staff.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to provide funding to community care organisations and PHIs to support them in keeping their salaries competitive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I also stressed the importance of ensuring the well-being of our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are working with clusters on measures to support the welfare and well-being of healthcare workers, including doctors and nurses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For doctors, this will include clearer work hour guidelines, reviews on work processes to improve efficiency and workload balancing and to enhance support for staff.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As the context differs from healthcare institutions, these changes may take time to effect.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On ensuring sufficient rest for nurses, our healthcare clusters no longer actively roster nurses on the PAPA shift pattern.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, this may happen occasionally when there are operational exigencies, such as when there is unplanned absence amongst staff and the ward needs to ensure the appropriate skills mix amongst nurses on duty to ensure patient safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: When this happens, measures are in place to support affected nurses, such as by rostering them on shorter shifts that week and allowing flexibility for swaps.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Additionally, we announced our tripartite framework on the prevention of abuse and harassment of healthcare workers and, in the coming year, we will be putting out additional publicity to raise awareness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I will now talk about our efforts to support Singaporeans to achieve healthier lifestyles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have supported Singaporeans in adopting healthier diets and an active lifestyle through various initiatives over the years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, we have introduced easy-to-use symbols and labels to help Singaporeans identify healthier products, and ensured access to healthier and affordable ingredients through the Healthier Ingredient Development Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A wide range of physical activities have also been provided island-wide.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are starting to see positive results from these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The National Nutrition Survey 2022 revealed that average daily sugar intake has decreased and more Singaporeans were meeting the recommended sugar limit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Participation rates in exercise programmes have also increased.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Despite these, we must remain vigilant about other health trends.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Based on the National Nutrition Survey, Singaporeans are eating more and 90% have exceeded the recommended daily limit of two grams of sodium.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We can make small shifts to incorporate healthier habits in our lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Continue to use the suite of user-friendly symbols and labels to make healthier purchases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Plan, monitor and moderate calorie intake using the Meal Log tool on the Healthy 365 app.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: When dining out, ask for less gravy and sauces and avoid drinking all the soup in soup-based dishes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Access a myriad of physical activities on the Healthy 365 app and participate in those of your liking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked about a Tobacco Cohort Ban.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The idea has been raised by several Members in the past.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our focus is on protecting public health and we do not rule out any measure that would help us achieve that effectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As Mr Giam pointed out, New Zealand had reversed their initial plans to implement a Tobacco Cohort Ban.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A salient point to note here is that New Zealand allows vaping and was prepared for people to switch from smoking to vaping.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: That leaves the UK, and we will monitor closely how they intend to implement the ban.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For a Tobacco Cohort Ban to be effective, we need to consider various implementation issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, can someone older buy cigarettes for someone younger who is affected by the ban?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: If not, how should we go about enforcing?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Giam mentioned that gains from existing measures have diminutive impact.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have made good progress in reducing smoking prevalence in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Hence, even as we study the feasibility of a Tobacco Cohort Ban, we will continue efforts to reduce smoking prevalence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As several Members and Singaporeans have raised, the emerging and urgent issue, is vaping.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There is a growing body of evidence that e-vaporisers are harmful, as they contain nicotine, a highly addictive substance, that can also harm the developing brains of youths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The cancer-causing chemicals and other toxic substances in e-vaporisers also increase the risk of heart and lung diseases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To Mr Ang and Dr Wan Rizal's questions, vaping is a multi-faceted issue and requires coordinated whole-of-Government efforts to tackle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH, along with the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) and the HPB, take a serious view on vaping.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The public can access information on the prohibition of e-vaporisers and its health harms across HSA and HPB's websites.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have worked across Ministries and agencies to step up enforcement and education measures, to protect our population and prevent e-vaporisers from taking hold in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Upstream, all sales and advertisements of e-vaporisers are prohibited under the law, in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Digital platform owners are expected to proactively moderate content by detecting and removing sales and advertisements of e-vaporisers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to work with the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) to engage platform owners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At the borders, HSA has worked with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) on a series of joint operations at Changi Airport, Woodlands and Tuas Checkpoints, and will continue to collaborate on a regular basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In the community, HSA is already working with agencies, such as the National Environment Agency (NEA) and National Parks Board (NParks), which have stepped up, and will continue to step up enforcement checks at public places.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In addition, the Singapore Police Force (SPF) and Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) continue to refer cases to HSA, when detected in the course of their duties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In schools and IHLs, MOE continues to take a firm stance against vaping and strengthen detection and enforcement efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Schools and IHLs take disciplinary actions against students caught using or possessing e-vaporisers, including suspension, or caning for boys in schools, and refer them to HSA for penalties under the law.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have also strengthened efforts on the education front to increase awareness about the harms and illegality of vaping.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In 2023, HPB launched a vape-free campaign targeted at youths and younger adults.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In schools, HPB has shared these messages with close to 90,000 students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parents, who are important stakeholders in this effort, are also kept up to date on the harms and illegality of vaping through advisories and resources available on Parent Hub.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to support those who smoke or vape to quit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Cessation programmes are accessible across various settings, including healthcare institutions, workplaces, uniformed services, education institutions and in the community, through initiatives, such as HPB's "I Quit" programme and Healthier SG.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I strongly urge all who are smoking or vaping to seek advice from a healthcare professional and quit as soon as possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Those with family or friends who smoke or vape should also encourage them to lead a nicotine-free lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Allow me to move on to talk about how we have strengthened targeted support as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With the roll-out of Healthier SG, in the Indian community, we have also partnered SINDA to set up a Health Task Force, comprising members from private and public healthcare institutions and other health-related organisations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to say a few words in Malay. :   In our Malay/Muslim community, we have recently introduced a focus area, which is FA5, "A Healthy Community for All".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This effort aims to promote healthier lifestyles and empower individuals and groups to organise and scale up community-led initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One key emphasis of FA5 is encouraging enrolment in Healthier SG in the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For those who are still contemplating whether to enrol or not, I would like to share how Healthier SG can be the next step in your preventive care journey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: She has also been actively participating in a variety of physical activities available on the Healthy 365 app, including Zumba, yoga, pilates and kickboxing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: You may be wondering how would an active resident, like Mdm Shamima, benefit further from enrolling in Healthier SG?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through her first Health Plan consultation with her family doctor, she is now more aware about her food intake and the importance of taking her medication on time, so that she can better manage her sugar levels.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through the regular follow-up consultations scheduled, her family doctor can provide her with guidance and encouragement to lead a healthier lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: FA5 will continue efforts to address key health issues in the Malay/Muslim community, such as screening, smoking and mental well-being, as Dr Wan Rizal mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will adopt a suitable approach for the Malay/Muslim community to achieve a more effective outcome. : Another dimension of providing targeted support is ensuring affordability, particularly for those who need it more.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We thank Members for your questions on how we are doing so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While these are not perfect proxies, they are the best available to measure an individual's means and family support, and only a small minority of long-term care clients do not qualify for subsidies because of the AV criterion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Seniors who face difficulties paying for their long-term care expenses may apply for the discretionary financial assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Second, Dr Tan Wu Meng has made two suggestions on empowering more organisations to assist with MediFund applications and taking a holistic approach to Migrant Domestic Worker Levy Concession applications.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We agree with the intent to smoothen help-seeking processes for needy patients.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is why, today, Singaporeans identified by Social Service Offices to receive ComCare assistance automatically receive MediFund assistance at approved healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have recently introduced guidelines to institutions to allow mutual recognition of MediFund assessments for more types of circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On the ground, institutions have also put in place patient-centric processes and leverage IT platforms to smoothen the application process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While tapping on other organisations could improve convenience of applying MediFund for some patients, it introduces an additional layer in the process and, therefore, needs to be studied further to avoid lengthening the application process inadvertently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As for the Migrant Domestic Worker Levy Concession, Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) remain a relevant basis for purposes of assessing these applications.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Frail patients with multiple conditions, or those at end-of-life, tend to require some assistance with at least one ADL and would qualify for the concession.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Exceptions will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to review the adequacy of financing schemes to support caregivers and their seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Regarding the case raised by Dr Tan, Dr Tan would be aware of the correspondences together by the AIC and Ms See.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There was a positive outcome after she was re-engaged by AIC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Unfortunately, there was an earlier miscommunication where AIC was led to believe that Ms See's cousin was the employer of the migrant domestic worker when it was, in fact, Ms See.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: She eventually qualified for and received the concession and Home Caregiving Grant, both backdated to when she qualified.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Third, to Mr Gerald Giam's question, we support the needs of persons with disabilities (PwDs) and persons with special needs through various financing schemes, including subsidies, national insurance schemes, MediSave, grants and safety nets, such as MediFund.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have recently enhanced some of these schemes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In general, healthcare subsidies are not based on specific conditions and are instead tiered based on income level, to target those who need more help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In the interim, those who face concerns may apply for discretionary funding support through MediFund or the Rare Disease Fund.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Lastly, a few Members have also asked about the support that is provided for those who are planning for a family.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There are a few considerations that guide our approach in designing the financing schemes to better support this group of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These include clinical safety and effectiveness of fertility tests and treatments, ensuring affordability for those who need it and keeping our financing schemes sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have answered Mr Louis Ng's question on support for fertility screening previously.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Fertility tests are offered to couples who are medically indicated as there is currently no evidence to support the need for early fertility checks for the general population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Those who face financial difficulties can also apply for MediFund for assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This offers more targeted support for those with needs, while safeguarding MediSave to ensure it remains adequate for other needs and keeping Central Provident Fund (CPF) contribution rates reasonable for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Currently, you can get an appointment at our public assisted reproduction centres for a first consult within a week, if you are open to seeing any of our IVF specialists.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To Mr Louis Ng's suggestion, we do not advise couples to switch providers after failed IVF cycles as it breaks the doctor-patient relationship, and may result in additional cost and time from repeated investigations and assessments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The outcomes of IVF treatments at private and public assisted reproduction centres are also comparable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To Ms Hazel Poa's ask for financial support for egg freezing, married women will be able to tap on co-funding and their MediSave when using their frozen eggs for assisted reproduction treatment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is to support couples who have decided to have a child, but may face challenges in conceiving.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We recognise the desire for women to freeze their eggs when they are young.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is a pre-emptive step, perhaps not different from buying private insurance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Providing financial support for it will be quite unprecedented in healthcare policy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We think it is better to focus our resources to directly help couples who are trying to conceive and who face difficulties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, I have shared about broad efforts to support Singaporeans in adopting healthier lifestyles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I have also shared about the targeted support for the ethnic minority groups and ensuring affordability for those who need it more, so that all Singaporeans can achieve better health and access care that they need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our efforts can only succeed with the strong participation of Singaporeans and support from families and the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are heartened that many have stepped up and made choices to lead a healthier lifestyle today, such as those who have enrolled in Healthier SG, made the switch to healthier eating, participated in healthy programmes and activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Let us choose better health for ourselves and our loved ones today.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: A question to the Minister on my cut.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second question pertains to my cut with regard to providing information beyond just the median vis-à-vis bed utilisation, and whether it can also be extended to bed utilisation at the 75th and 90th percentiles.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Is this a significant problem in the hospitals?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It would be helpful if the Minister could share some information on overstayers and whether there could be better coordination between medical social workers and the consultants and overseeing doctors, so that this problem can be abated somewhat.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The definition of "urgent care" is actually standardised and practised.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have a nomenclature P1, P2 which are considered urgent; P3 onwards not so urgent and it goes up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, therefore, this is based on a standard definition, and so P3 and above is 40%.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do not have the number on whether it is stable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am hoping it has come down over time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, even if it is tracked over time, it may not be representative.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we are doing what we can educating the public, having UCCs, having GPFirst programme to reduce this number.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, our concerns still stand, that the worry is that with dynamic information, we are encouraging more P3s, non-urgent, from coming to EDs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Sometimes, when the ED has a breather, maybe we should just let the doctors and nurses have a breather.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But as I said, we are not rejecting the suggestion, but we always had this concern.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for bed waiting time beyond median, whether we can indicate 75th, 90th percentile, the issue remains this: that if there is urgent care needed, it will be given almost immediately, without delay, at the ED if possible.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I take Mr Singh's point that it is not the most comfortable place.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is a trolley bed, but it is not a proper ward.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Those who need urgent care in the ward, we will give them immediately.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it is not just a matter of waiting time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The urgency and the clinical needs of the patient play a big part as well.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We know that day surgery lowers the cost, as compared to an in-hospital stay, if they undergo some form of surgery.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Would MOH be willing to explore to see how to expand day surgery, to change it to an outpatient surgery model instead?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Which means that they do not have that 24-hour limit that is currently in place now.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If we can extend it to 36 hours or 72 hours, that will actually allow us to have a bigger range of procedures to be done as day surgery.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I think that is proven for a long time already.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The second supplementary question is on healthcare cost.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We are concerned with healthcare cost increases because the total household medical expenditure will go up, whether it is premium from insurance, whether it is their MediSave or whether it is out of pocket, because out of all these three, these three will continue to go up.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We are just after the US and Hong Kong.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I hope that we will not climb further and overtake Hong Kong.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I understand that MediShield Life premium is under review now.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Then last of all, for MediSave, it is still our money.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: MediSave uses have been expanded a lot now, including hospitalisation, clinic uses now, health screening cost.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Is the current MediSave amount that we have now sufficient in consideration of an ageing population, as well as increased lifespan?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I fully agree with Dr Lim on the importance of day surgery.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Without our push to convert many surgeries to day surgeries or even shortened stays, the impact actually would have been far worse.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we managed to contain it to six to seven days.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And we will continue to work on this front.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As of now, we think it is quite adequate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we will continue to monitor the situation, especially if we cannot contain the rise in premiums.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Then, I think the drain on MediSave will be quite significant.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But it is something we will have to monitor.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Dr Lim asked a couple of questions on MediShield Life, private insurance as well as premium.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What I just announced and talked about is to reduce healthcare cost.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Healthcare cost is increased not just because of insurance premium.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is the whole purpose of this exercise.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Increase the claim limits, so that healthcare cost for them is manageable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Of course, this comes with an impact on MediShield Life premiums.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But as I mentioned, we will try our best to help them pay for it through their MediSave.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I mentioned a few things that we can do: increase subsidies, do top-ups for specific groups if possible, find ways so that we can all manage.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I think this is a better way to manage healthcare costs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These are private and commercially run insurance premiums and they have been going up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am unaware that we have the third highest premiums in the world.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think we have to be comparing apples to apples, oranges to oranges, because it depends on what kind of insurance plans are they.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I really hope that, at some point, they will rein this in and exercise more discipline so that we also moderate private insurance premiums.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: My clarifications are for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am glad to hear that the Government does not rule out a generational smoking ban.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask whether the Government is actively moving forward on this plan and what is the timeline it is looking at?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: For the sake of the health of our future generations, I hope that we can move faster and be an early mover on this and not wait for other countries.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: But first, does the Senior Parliamentary Secretary agree that this is not the case for the Pioneer and Merdeka Generation who get additional subsidies regardless of their income status?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, can this be applied as well to PwDs?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And second, does healthcare means-testing always take into account the many other expenses that PwDs incur for their daily living, which will lower their ability to pay for healthcare regardless of their family income?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As you can see from the results and the outcomes, we are doing quite well as compared to other places.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In deciding what are some of the measures and approaches that we take, we really have to look at things in totality.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We looked at taxes, we looked at standardised packaging, we increased the minimum legal age; and this has actually to a large extent, shown very good results.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the other hand, as we are assessing the tobacco cohort ban, we are looking at the outcomes in other places and it may not necessarily generate the same outcome that we want.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, I think it will take some time for us to assess whether there are other measures that are going to change this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And on that front, there are some more salient points or more imperative issues that we need to deal with, with regard to vaping for example.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we do need to focus our energies in dealing with some of those emergent issues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Your second question related to the support for the PwDs, I appreciate the point and I can understand.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In fact, this is something I also raised with other Ministries, in terms of support for PwDs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We do really have to look at appropriate circumstances.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: At the moment, a lot of the support that we have given, we have looked at enhancing as it goes along.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And I can say, as a general principle, if there are specific issues of families who need help, we have our tiered-support system where they can definitely get the help they need.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Having said that, I think this is something that we will continue to look at and see, where appropriate, we can continue to enhance.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I have a clarification for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu on vaping.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Could Senior Parliamentary Secretary share, how many cases of feedback that the HSA received from the public, from the police and from the CNB respectively in 2023?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: And can she share, what is the size of the enforcement team at HSA and what is your assessment of the effectiveness of the enforcement action by HSA?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: These are the questions I have asked in my cuts.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do not have the numbers with me, but you are right, vaping is a problem.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And more and more people, especially the young, are vaping.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And it is not just us, it is around the world.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu explained a holistic way of tackling the problem.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We can collaborate with the ICA to do enforcement at the border; but we rely on NEA, on NParks Board and other agencies, to help us enforce this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think if our enforcement officers can multi-task and I think we can mount a fairly effective enforcement against vaping.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: She mentioned CTGTP as a treatment option for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) patients.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: While I appreciate that this may be true, to my understanding, it benefits young children rather than adults.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Risdiplam seems to be the way to go for adults with SMA.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I do not mean to press MOH on this, but SMA patients are really keen on this treatment which works to preserve their quality of life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: With regard to the Member's question, I note his point and actually beyond just the CTGTP, we are also looking at the effectiveness of treatments that are not in that field.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I take the Member's point, and I think this is something we can consider and look at, as we are engaging with the pharmaceutical companies.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: For the Second Minister for Health, Minister Masagos; and two questions for Minister Ong.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I am really very glad about the expansions of AACs.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I wanted to ask, in the selection for the social service agency or the operator for the new AAC, will the Ministry or AIC put more considerations on existing agencies who are already operating existing AAC in the constituency?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Because many times, they have already built very good relationships with the grassroots organisations and it is very important for local collaborations as more AACs emerge in the constituency.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: The two questions for Minister Ong are: firstly, on the MIC@Home going to become a mainstream care option.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I think it is good news, but the move from its pilot state to mainstream is relatively faster than a lot of the healthcare pilots that we know about.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I wanted to ask, how will the quality of care and patient safety be monitored and assured as this option begins to scale-up nationwide, especially if there are situations of disputes and responsibility of roles between the families and the care team?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: My final question is on the MediShield Life review that is upcoming and the premium that may be adjusted.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: One of the objectives for Healthier SG when it was first announced, was to blunt the healthcare cost increases that we are seeing internationally as well as in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: But Healthier SG is in its very early phases; and I wanted to ask, how would the Council for the review take into consideration of the cost-blunting effect of Healthier SG in the review that is coming up?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And of course, they must have a good track record in engaging or serving residents living in the area among other criteria that will be considered.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: How to ensure quality of care of MIC@Home is maintained?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Which is why I explained, from 100 to 300 institutions; feel this is something they can cope and they can maintain the quality.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are not even one year and this is really a long-term strategy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Hopefully, towards the end of this decade, we can see a blunting or bending of the cost curve as we call it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And at that point in time, of course, we will then take that effect into account as we conduct further reviews of the MediShield Life scheme.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As the Minister has pointed out, healthcare costs have risen.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, are there plans to revise the MediSave withdrawal limits?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the Minister consider annual adjustments pegged to healthcare inflation similar to the way the basic retirement sum is reviewed?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If I heard her correctly, I would just like to clarify that this is already being done in countries, like South Korea, Japan, Australia and France.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: MediShield Life limits withdrawal, I assume you meant for outpatient.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For outpatient, we review it from time to time and we have been adjusting over the years.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But as for MediSave limits that you can withdraw for big hospital bills, I think there needs to be corresponding adjustments.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Sorry, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu, you wanted to add something?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is unprecedented with regard to our health policy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: While we note that this is something that is being done elsewhere, we are monitoring.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are looking at the data from abroad and we see that the take-up rate from overseas is also very low.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Also, even if it is taken up, there is also evidence that suggests that the outcomes necessarily may not be very good.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, these are some of the considerations that we take into account.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But when I meant unprecedented, it is unprecedented within our healthcare policy.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I echo Ms Ng Ling Ling's query on what exactly does this MIC@Home look like from the caregiver's perspective; and whether the Government will consider that for those families where family members have to involuntarily give up employment to assume caregiving duties at home, given that it is skill-intensive and helps to supplement the formal health care system, whether care fare can be considered as an income supplement?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I have met residents who say even though the family receives home caregiving grants, they do not feel like they can take that money from their elderly parents because there is a grant given to the care recipient.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These are all things that we will continue to review and as described by the Second Minister.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I would just like to pick up on the point the Minister shared about the 40% of ED cases being non-critical.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Of course, to be fair, I recognise that such behaviour is not unique to Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In the US, ERs are often also flooded by overuse, albeit with different reasons that have to do with the uninsured.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My suggestion for expanding UCCs is, therefore, I think, both complementary but distinct to the question of capacity in general.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My first question then is, if MOH agrees that UCCs can indeed be a complementary part of the secondary-care landscape, how do we increase their take-up?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: What sort of incentives or educational efforts can MOH provide to non-urgent cases to choose to access UCCs instead of our EDs?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My second question relates to his point about the doctor-to-population ratio.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: He shared that Japan has a comparable ratio in the face of a large elderly population.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But I would venture that European countries, which he mentioned, are in fact better-prepared in terms of medical staffing for their super-aged societies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: On that, I wonder if MOH will consider increasing the number of medical schools that it recognises from foreign countries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: After all, as he said, the competition for talent is global and so, it seems unnecessary for us to further hamstring our efforts to recruit from abroad.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do not think we should describe as, whether MOH agrees that UCCs are useful.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And as I mentioned, if need be, if we need to set up more UCCs – this is a proven model – we will consider doing so.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: GPFirst in the east has also worked quite well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, between the two, either or, I think we should consider them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for doctor-to-population ratio, I explained to some extent in my speech, the European doctor-to-population ratio is somehow just higher than the rest of the world.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Even in Asia, comparing developed economies, we are more or less about the same level.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do not know what is the reason, some say it is the legacy of the welfare state, others say they did not plan for manpower.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But when you look at individual European countries, it is not that pretty a picture.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Dutch, for example, they have stopped using nursing homes because there are not enough medical personnel nor doctors to man them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, today, if you are an old person in Holland, in Netherlands, the default care model is actually home care with a lay person, maybe a nurse, maybe an allied professional visiting you twice or three times a day.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Germany, the doctors there told me they are in dire straits.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Across the states, the hospitals are not efficiently configured and that is what they told me and therefore they are also, despite having more doctors, not delivering the healthcare that the people need.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, as I mentioned, it is just one number.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Where they are trained and what kind of specialty, how the entire system is run, whether the insurance system of that country or the welfare system is creating oversupply, all these play a part.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So we take all these into consideration as we manage our healthcare challenge.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Ten years ago, it was about 2.0, today it is 2.6.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, moving forward, there is some room for three local medical schools to take in slightly more perhaps.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is possibility of having more overseas-trained Singaporean doctors returning, all these we have to consider.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Our ratio has been increasing, we are ageing, most likely we will increase further.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I would just caution the European model may not be the model that we want to emulate fully.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am heartened to hear that there are many initiatives to help our seniors age well in the community.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First is on the National Silver Academy (NSA), which offers many useful courses for learning for seniors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, awareness of the courses and training are still quite spotty on the ground.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: So, how can we improve awareness and take-up rate amongst our seniors for these courses?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, I am glad to note that the waiting time for nursing homes is about one month.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Minister mentioned that there are interim care options for those who are on the waitlist.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can he share what are these options and how can caregivers get access to these options?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The agency, or the body, that runs and takes care of this programme is the Council for Third Age and we will work with them, as suggested by the Member, to increase even more awareness about the programmes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They will do this through the usual publicity channels like social media, roadshows, community touchpoints, partnership events.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, even the annual National Celebration of Seniors events will be one marquee event, where they will be present and to bring up the awareness of the availability of all these programmes that our seniors can meet their aspirations and their interests.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They can be referred to the transitional care facilities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In nine hospitals, they are available and I hope that residents or caregivers of these patients can go and meet up with the staff at these centres, where they can provide both plans for short-term post discharge, as well as the longer-term needs of their parents or the people they are caring for.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Heartened to see that safety as well as outcomes are comparable as it stands today, but Minister also mentioned that in terms of pricing, it is expected to be the same or less.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I am just wondering whether, at least in my mind, should it not be less pricing in absolute terms, given that the care is based now at home and auxiliary services, such as the bed, change in linen, meals, utilities would be much less.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I appreciate there are other costs, but I wonder whether the Minister could clarify that.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The second is on the planned increase for COMIT as well as CREST.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I think a greater increase of COMIT and CREST teams would give some confidence to our GPs on the ground, in terms of dealing with mental health issues in the community.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: MIC@Home, I pay less; plus I have S+3M, hospital bill will be less.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So our public health institutions take this to heart, they understand and I think they are prepared to do so.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I wrote a careful statement that the price will be equal or less, so to give them some room.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: What we do not really know is what the behaviour of patients and residents, people who are concerned about mental health behaviour; how that will change over the next 10 to 15 years as we are increasing our CREST and COMIT teams.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think we need to ramp up the support available for the private and public sector practitioners in the community space, increase the number of teams, the capability of the teams that we have.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But how that goes and how that matches with health-seeking behaviour, the worried well, the people who need interventions, people who have been in institutional care, who now need to come into the community; these are things that we will be monitoring and watching very closely through the NMHO and working with our partners and then assessing whether we have the right level of support.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, I agree with the sentiment, but I think it is a little bit too early to say now what we will be doing in 2030.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We get going with our current plans first.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Your clarifications were concise and so, too, were the responses.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, can I invite Dr Tan if you would like to draw your amendment?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Mr Chairman, I want to thank all who contributed to the COS debate, our MOH leadership and office holders and our Members of Parliament, our Members of Parliament who spoke as well.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Deepest thanks to our entire healthcare family as well, our healthcare workers; our sisters and brothers, who care for patients and residents in the community; our public officers, who worked tirelessly behind the scenes looking after Singaporeans, in sickness and in health.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
